## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Treatment Product
where: TreatmentService (uses), src/business/treatmentService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
return this.products.create({ name: productName, withdrawalDays });
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B

=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: A and B are different concepts. A, Treatment Product, is a catalog item: the code creates it with a name and withdrawal days (`this.products.create({ name: productName, withdrawalDays })`). It is stored in its own TreatmentProductRepository. B, Treatment, is an event in which a product is applied to a hive. Its records are kept in TreatmentRepository (`private readonly items: TreatmentRecord[]`). TreatmentService (node 2912145e8ad12343) calls both repositories as separate dependencies. It looks up treatments by hive (TreatmentRepository.findByHive) but looks up products by name (TreatmentProductRepository.findByName). So a product is a reusable definition, and a treatment is one recorded use of a product on a hive. The two are related, but they are not the same thing under different names.
